key_insight: A small set of attention heads helps determine whether a multimodal AI follows images or text when they disagree. These “arbitration heads” offer a targeted way to influence which evidence the model uses.
problem_solved: Multimodal large language models can favor the wrong source of information when visual and textual inputs conflict, making their answers unreliable.
method: Study how models choose between visual and textual evidence under conflicting inputs.
Identify attention heads that causally influence whether predictions follow images or text.
Use these heads as targets for inference-time control; the provided abstract is truncated before the full control method is described.
impact: This work points toward more controllable multimodal systems that can prioritize appropriate evidence when inputs disagree. The supplied excerpt does not include results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: An image–text conflict example with contradictory labels feeding into one model.
A model schematic highlighting a small set of arbitration heads.
A visual-versus-textual evidence dial illustrating inference-time control.
A flowchart linking conflicting inputs, arbitration heads, and the model’s final choice.
paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
